newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields see a small recoil upwards.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields see a small recoil upwards.

text.p: Swedish debt markets saw a slight recoil on Monday and the crown was a little weaker against a generally stronger D-mark.
"We have seen a small recoil. There has been some profit-taking from the recent gains," one trader said.
The spread against Germany increased by 3 basis points to 90 points. Most traders Reuters spoke to said this is primarily due to a recoil from the narrowing trend of late.
The ten-year bond yield rose 2 basis points to 6.49 percent while the December T-bill rose 2 basis points to 4.11 percent.

The mark is said to be generally stronger in a recoil. The crown therefore was somewhat weaker to 4.4140 from 4.4070 late on Friday. The crown is expected to trade between 4.3900 to 4.4250 against the mark today.
Trading was very light on the debt market as well as in the forex market, according to dealers.
